strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy linalg accuracy bug for `scipy.linalg.pinvh` on the buggy revision (commit 237b6915e37e) where `pinvh` can rely on `eigh` using the LAPACK SYEVR/`evr` path, producing a perturbed near-zero eigenvalue and causing the Moore–Penrose condition 2 (`allclose(a @ p @ a, a)`) to fail for a specific Hermitian matrix. Ensure the project test `test_zero_eigenvalue` fails on buggy and passes on fixed by checking out the buggy commit vs the fixed PR head.

pinned_because: SciPy constraint is documented as 1.4.1 and NumPy as 1.18.1 (issue#12515 reproduction context).
Python 3.7.6 matches the provided environment; LAPACK driver behavior (SYEVR vs SYEV) can be sensitive, so keep this environment stable.

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 237b6915e37e, `test_zero_eigenvalue` fails because the second Moore–Penrose check `assert_allclose(a @ p @ a, a, atol=1e-15)` is false. On the fixed revision (PR #20297 includes changing `pinvh` to call `eigh(..., driver='ev')` / using SYEV instead of SYEVR), the same test passes (both `assert_allclose(p @ a @ p, p, atol=1e-15)` and `assert_allclose(a @ p @ a, a, atol=1e-15)` succeed).
strategy.numerical_probe: Matrix a = [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]]; compute p = scipy.linalg.pinvh(a); verify Moore–Penrose conditions via np.allclose/allclose tolerance atol=1e-15.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: For y1 = pinvh(x): np.allclose(x @ y1 @ x, x) == True but np.allclose(y1 @ x @ y1, y1) == False.
input_output_examples.expected_output: For p = pinvh(a) the test expects both Moore–Penrose conditions to satisfy allclose with atol=1e-15, i.e., np.allclose(p @ a @ p, p, atol=1e-15) and np.allclose(a @ p @ a, atol=1e-15) are True.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: driver='evr' may report a zero eigenvalue as approximately 2.66453526e-15 (shown example) vs driver='ev' approximately 9.99658224e-17.
input_output_examples.expected_output: Using the more robust SYEV/`ev` path avoids the larger perturbation of the near-zero eigenvalue, yielding a correct `pinvh` pseudoinverse for the test matrix.

risks: This is LAPACK-driver sensitive: the failure depends on whether `pinvh` ends up using the SYEVR (`evr`) path for `eigh` in the buggy revision. If your build/linked LAPACK version or SciPy’s internal driver selection causes SYEV-like behavior even on the buggy commit, the test may pass (no transition).
Exact behavior can vary by platform/architecture, BLAS/LAPACK vendor, and threading/runtime; only attempt the comparison on the same environment/toolchain for buggy vs fixed commits.

The evidence does not specify compiler flags, BLAS/LAPACK backend, or exact PR fixed commit SHA; you must test on the same checkout baseline except for the code change from PR #20297 (driver selection in `scipy/linalg/_basic.py`).

oracle.reference_source: Embedded test in scipy/linalg/tests/test_basic.py (added in PR #20297) using assert_allclose for the two Moore–Penrose conditions.
oracle.why: The test asserts both Moore–Penrose conditions with an absolute tolerance of 1e-15; the buggy behavior is characterized as failing the condition `assert_allclose(a @ p @ a, a, atol=1e-15)` while still passing `assert_allclose(p @ a @ p, p, atol=1e-15)`.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: `pytest ... -k test_zero_eigenvalue` raises an AssertionError at `assert_allclose(a @ p @ a, a, atol=1e-15)` (second Moore–Penrose condition fails) for `a = [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]]` because the buggy revision’s driver path for `eigh` yields a near-zero eigenvalue that is not treated accurately enough for `pinvh`.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: `pytest ... -k test_zero_eigenvalue` succeeds because the fix changes `pinvh` to use the more robust SYEV/`ev` driver in `eigh`, avoiding the larger perturbation from SYEVR/`evr` and restoring the Moore–Penrose condition `allclose(a @ p @ a, a, atol=1e-15)`.
